shouldFix.title: The recording drops the Codex advisory provenance instead of explicitly de-duplicating the shared finding
shouldFix.finding: The draft cites the Codex v3 verdict at digest 0bb9f9c8... and correctly reports ACCEPT at 0 blockers / 0 SHOULD-FIX, but Decision 3 says only 'Claude advisories from the v3 ACCEPT travel as honesty work.' The cited Codex verdict has one advisory, POOCV3-ADV1. It is substantively the same parked-identity-dependency-routing class as Claude's CLAUDE-POOC-V3-ADV-2, while Claude also has distinct CLAUDE-POOC-V3-ADV-1. Thus no distinct substantive class is lost, but one independent review's finding ID and provenance disappear from the durable recording with no stated de-duplication. The corpus has an exact same-class precedent: D-106 names CLAUDE-V6-A1 / CODEX-V6-A1 and says they are one advisory class rather than silently retaining only one reviewer ID.
shouldFix.whyNotMustFix: The omitted Codex advisory adds no distinct remediation: its substance is already carried by the Claude-advisories clause through CLAUDE-POOC-V3-ADV-2. The dual 0/0 acceptance, authority boundary, candidate recording, and readiness arithmetic remain correct. This is review-record fidelity, not a defect in the decision's core effect.

coordinatorSummary: OBJECT at 0 MUST-FIX and 1 SHOULD-FIX. All five prompt attacks are otherwise refuted. Subject custody held at b4b4b475... mode 0444; every measured input and HEAD pin reproduces. v3 is genuinely dual ACCEPT at 0 blockers / 0 SHOULD-FIX: Claude carries two advisories and Codex one. The decision correctly records only an accepted candidate, leaves DR-133 OPEN, opens no D-056 Class A because both verdicts are candidate-only rather than application-grade T2-02 acceptance, changes no file-08 status, leaves readiness 4 of 32, and grants no implementation, application, seal, qualification, or D-096 authority. The sole defect is the durability of the review record. Decision 3 carries only 'Claude advisories', while the cited Codex verdict contains POOCV3-ADV1. That Codex advisory duplicates Claude's second advisory, so no distinct remediation is lost and blocker grade would be excessive; nevertheless the independent ID/provenance is silently dropped and no same-class de-duplication is stated. D-106 supplies the exact precedent: name both reviewer IDs and record that they are one class. A turn-2 sentence doing that should clear this review without changing the decision's substance or readiness effect.
